text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Shareholders' lobby group VEB set to claim Dfl 60 million from management and supervisory board of Bobel. (p1)
- Capital managers brace for share price corrections in near future. (p1)
- Groningen-based cable-TV operator CasTel in deal with U.S. WorldCom to provide international telecom services in north and eastern Netherlands. (p1)
- Industrial gas maker Hoek Loos to partly finance takeover of U.S. rival Sunox with Dfl 100 million share issue. (p1)
- Van Dorp announces losses for current book year. (p3)
- Coffee roaster Drie Mollen discusses takeover of three European rivals from Israeli food group Elith. (p4)
- Han Kleiterp to become supervisory board president of company formed from merger of Amsterdam Stock Exchange and Amsterdam Options Exchange from Jan 1. (p13)
VOLKSKRANT
- Sports-only commercial TV station Sport 7 abandons, for at least a year, plans to make viewers pay. (p1)
- Nine utility companies refuse to cooperate with automation firm Multihouse in developing consumer information system Numis-2000. (p2)
- Financial services group SNS Group ends 140 agencies. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- South Korean industrial conglomerate Samsung to decide today on taking over aircraft maker Fokker. (p1)
- Chip Market Europe claims hundreds of millions of guilders from Akzo Nobel over production methods for solar cells. (p13)
- Capital market interest rates rise slightly. (p13)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Dutch computer users take fourth place in western European ranking of illegal software use. (p1)
- Run on entertainment company Endemol's shares. (p11)
TROUW
- Schiphol president-director believes "unorthodox" methods should be used to build second national airport as soon as possible (p1)
- Labour faction chairman does not want decision on Beek airport's nightflight regime to be taken this week. (p3)
